## Codex adaptation and security boundary

This is a per-turn native Codex guidance adapter. It preserves the 23 playbooks and their principles, but it does not create a sticky mode or claim implicit future invocation. Read the selected playbook from the project-local mirror. Map the upstream question action to the host's optional user-input surface only for a genuine product or preference choice. Map the upstream task and delegation fields to native bounded delegation when exposed, keeping scope, selected model/effort, ownership, and proof with the coordinator. If named delegation is unavailable, report the exact gap; sequential local work may continue, but it does not complete the named-role playbook step. For cleanup, use `cursor-deslop` when installed; for CLI/TUI surfaces, use `cursor-control-cli`; for browser/Electron/web surfaces, use `cursor-control-ui`. Check each concrete skill before use and record the exact gap when unavailable or not applicable. Cloud-capable task environments are conditional; if the cloud lane is unavailable, record the gap and do not claim parity. Keep model selection with model-capability-router and proof-path selection with proof-orchestrator. A heartbeat or automation is used only when explicitly requested. Ordinary playbook delegates call native `collaboration.spawn_agent` with `agent_type: "poteto-agent"` when that exact type is exposed; reuse an existing suitable named agent with `collaboration.followup_task` instead of spawning a sibling. The profile is distributed by `model-capability-router`; install it explicitly before a fresh Codex session can select it. If the exact type is unavailable, report the gap and leave named-role execution incomplete rather than substituting a generic agent. Read the selected `cursor-principle-*` leaf when applied. Routed workflow skills (`cursor-how`, `cursor-why`, `cursor-interrogate`, `cursor-reflect`, `cursor-swarm`, `cursor-architect`, and `cursor-arena`) keep their own role-specific contracts. Reuse the same named delegate when supported. Automatic sticky routing, fresh top-level profile loading, and full live playbook execution remain unproven; native selection and bounded follow-up of a named `poteto-agent` have been observed in this task tree.

This skill is published and indexed for explicit invocation. Installing it makes the guidance, playbooks, references, and reviewed profile dependency available; it does not authorize the bundled Bun/TypeScript CLI, dependency installation, real-repository mutation, or GitHub access. Those executable surfaces remain separately gated. The detailed fixture and security evidence stays in `MIRROR.md`; it is historical proof, not an active installation prohibition.
codex_rule: Respect native Codex model/effort, permissions and actual tool availability; no automatic Cursor runtime equivalence.
preserved_requirement: poteto's agent style for concise, detailed responses, deliberate subagents, unslopped prose, simple code, and verified work. Use for poteto, /poteto-mode, or requests to work in this style.
proof: Pinned source hash and deterministic renderer are static provenance. Focused tests render the held candidate, verify all 23 playbook files and native-boundary metadata, structurally read the exact `bug-fix` playbook, and execute a synthetic notes app through contextual before/failure/trace/plan/local-history/prewritten-correction/after steps with independent stdout/exit evidence. The local Git fixture proves reproduction-before-fix commit ordering and a temporary local bare remote simulation, never a real PR. A negative case proves the correction is not written when the failure evidence is not exact; marker, unexpected-entry, and Git-timeout guards are also tested. Fixture-local portions of source steps 1/4/5 were exercised; 2/3/6 are partial (bounded hypothesis and structural diff record, no architect/delegation/review, and simulation only). Safe checks execute read-only `check-plan.mjs`, mocked `worktree-audit.sh`, five dependency-free `orch/store.ts` operations in scratch, and real `watch-pr/github.ts` command wiring against mocked `gh`/`git` under an outer timeout. One approved exact-lock scratch install used `--frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` and verified commander 14.0.0, bun-types 1.3.14, typescript 7.0.2, @types/node 26.1.2, and undici-types 8.3.0; a fresh no-`node_modules` scratch then exercised the real missing-key bootstrap install/restart from that populated cache, created the install key, and ran real `orch` and `watch-pr` CLIs. A separate authorized status-only read of real PR #64 exited 0 with empty stderr and returned raw `reviewDecision=REVIEW_REQUIRED`, `isDraft=true`, `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED`, CI `SUCCESS` on head `f5a77fa0`; its `Review ✅` cell is explicitly not review approval because `render.ts` checks threads/automation, while the policy now blocks `REVIEW_REQUIRED` in the adapted preview. The cache run was not network-instrumented, the key does not verify package version, and mocks plus an external timeout bounded other git/GitHub subprocesses. The initial pre-population offline probe failed because those pins were absent from the original cache. The result is `FIXTURE_ONLY`; it does not prove contextual behavior on the live target, that the playbook generated the correction, polling/stack behavior, merge readiness, cloud task execution, or a live native session. The pinned poteto-agent source remains in the snapshot and the public native profile asset is byte-matched. A named native `poteto-agent` was selected and reused through follow-up in this task tree for a bounded Eval readback, but full playbook execution and exact model/effort metadata were not established. The critical-script review is static plus safe-subset/scratch proof only and the hold remains. The public native poteto-agent TOML has a source-hash-checked exact body adaptation and installed-byte check; fresh top-level session loading and automatic skill trigger remain unproven.
reason: The adapter preserves the full source tree while making the runtime mapping, no-sticky boundary, native authority, and executable-script hold explicit.
